
The generated functions in `stashapi` map directly to Stash GraphQL
operations. The snake_case helpers compose those operations for recurring
workflows without hiding the underlying API.

## Resolve a named object

Use the explicit helpers when a script needs an ID for an exact name:

```r
studio_id <- find_studio_id("Example Studio")
tag_id <- find_tag_id("moderators")
performer_id <- find_performer_id("Example Performer")
```

If an exact name has multiple matches, the default is to stop rather than pick
one silently. Choose deliberately when that is appropriate:

```r
find_tag_id("Example Tag", multiple = "first")
find_tag_id("Example Tag", multiple = "all")
```

## Wait for a job

Long-running operations return a job ID. `wait_for_job()` polls until the job
finishes and returns the final job record:

```r
job_id <- metadataScan(input = list(paths = "/data/Images"))
job <- wait_for_job(job_id, check_interval = 30, timeout = 3600)
```

Failed, cancelled, unknown, and timed-out jobs raise errors. Set
`verbose = FALSE` when the surrounding script provides its own progress UI.

## Find tag descendants

Tag hierarchies can be queried server-side with a parent criterion. The helper
makes that intent explicit and requests all pages:

```r
positions_id <- find_tag_id("positions")
positions_tags <- tag_descendants(positions_id)
```

The default result has the same shape as `findTags()`, including the standard
`id` column. Request only IDs when they will be reused in another filter:

```r
positions_tag_ids <- tag_descendants(
  moderators_id,
  .field = c("tags", "id")
)

images <- findImages(
  imagefilter = image_filter(
    tags = includes(positions_tag_ids)
  ),
  filter = find_filter(per_page = -1)
)
```

Limit the hierarchy depth when unlimited traversal is unnecessary:

```r
direct_and_second_level <- tag_descendants(positions_id, depth = 2)
```

Include the root tag when the workflow needs the complete branch:

```r
complete_branch <- tag_descendants(
  positions_id,
  include_self = TRUE
)
```

`tag_descendants()` uses the server-side `parents` filter. It does not walk
children recursively in R, assign tags, or resolve names. Use `find_tag_id()`
separately when starting from a name so duplicate-name behavior remains
explicit.

## Common operation options

The generated operation functions remain available when a helper does not fit
the workflow. Helpers forward the same response options where applicable:

```r
tag_descendants(
  positions_id,
  .field = c("tags", "id"),
  .progress_bar = TRUE
)
```

The helper functions are intentionally small. Path parsing, matching local
files to Stash objects, metadata policy, and mutation decisions remain in the
users script.
